title: Exceptional coefficient construction: finite scalar mates
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ with $k=\overline{k_0}$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $R_E$, uniformizers $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=R_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism; neither $X$ nor $Y$ is assumed separated over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow{p_c}Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Write $\mathcal C_{T,A}=D^b_{ctf}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for the actual full category of bounded constructible constant-$A$ complexes with finite Tor amplitude, and $I_{T,A}$ for its full inclusion [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Put $F_A=Rp_{c,*}j_!$ and $G_A=\nu_X^*f^\times_{c,A}R\nu_{Y,*}$, using the ordinary etale compact-support right adjoint [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Equip these functors with the transported adjunction and adjoint shift structures. For every unital finite coefficient map $a:A\to B$ between the rings $A_{E,n}$ (including quotients and ramified maps $A_{E,n}\to A_{L,en}$), the ambient derived extension $S_{a,T}=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ preserves $\mathcal C_{T,A}$ and its Tor interval. It admits the literal full-subcategory restriction $T_{a,T}$, so $I_{T,B}T_{a,T}=S_{a,T}I_{T,A}$ is an equality of functors and its realization is the equality isomorphism. There are invertible shift-compatible comparisons
$$q_a:T_{a,Y}F_A\xrightarrow{\sim}F_BT_{a,X},\qquad b_a:T_{a,X}G_A\xrightarrow{\sim}G_BT_{a,Y}.$$
The first is exactly the proper scalar-adjunction mate followed by the open tensor map, transported from etale to pro-etale by the canonical proper/open comparisons. The second is the $F_B\dashv G_B$ transpose of $T_{a,Y}\epsilon_A\circ q_{a,G_A}^{-1}$, so
$$\epsilon_{B,T_{a,Y}L}\circ F_B(b_{a,L})\circ q_{a,G_AL}=T_{a,Y}(\epsilon_{A,L}).$$
This assertion includes nonflat quotients. On restriction of scalars the right map is the constant-$B$ exceptional tensor comparison, through the canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{Res}_XG_B\cong G_A\operatorname{Res}_Y$. All realizations use the same counits, site-comparison units and flat-model pullback/tensor identifications; the proper projection and open maps preserve their shifts.
